title: Scarlet Oak: Ancient Scarlet Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: The eastern American oak planted for its red autumn crown. Mount Auburn's grew wild before the cemetery opened in 1831 and is close to 32 metres tall.
intro: Scarlet oak is a North American oak grown in parks for its autumn crown, which turns a deep red. The oldest of ours was not planted at all. Mount Auburn Cemetery, outside Boston, opened in 1831 around one that was already growing wild by what is now Moss Path, and its inventory gives that tree 4.07 metres of trunk and a height close to 32 metres. Massachusetts lists a champion scarlet oak somewhere in the cemetery, and nobody has settled whether it is this one. In Seattle, a street tree at a Wedgwood corner cracked in a March 2016 windstorm and was cabled and braced instead of felled, with hardware rated to 54,000 pounds. And in Arnhem, the monumental tree register dates a scarlet oak to around 1900 to 1910, in the Velperplein park laid over a filled-in canal, where it came through the square's complete rebuilding between 1995 and 2005.
